title: What to watch at the open
text: Thursday was a rough day: all 17 names on our list closed lower. Overnight, stock markets in Asia fell too, led by AI and chip companies. Today, watch whether AI chip stocks like NVIDIA and AMD keep falling or start to steady. Also watch the dividend fund SCHD and Lockheed Martin, which fell the least on Thursday.

title: NVIDIA starts the day at its 52 week low
text: NVIDIA closed Thursday at $145.98, just above its lowest price of the past year ($145.71). AP reported it was up 4.7% early in the day before it flipped to a 3.3% loss. It is now 40% below its 52 week high. A price near the low tells us where it sits, not where it goes next.

title: AI supplies fell more than AI giants
text: On Thursday our 'AI supplies' group (NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, Vertiv, AMD) fell about 4.2% on average. The 'AI giants' group (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) fell about 3.1%. Chip and equipment makers depend more directly on AI spending, so they tend to swing harder in both directions.

title: Rocket Lab and Vertiv carry the highest risk scores
text: Rocket Lab's risk score is 10 out of 10 and Vertiv's is 8.1. Both have high beta, which means they usually move much more than the overall market. Rocket Lab is 66% below its 52 week high and Vertiv is 51% below. Big swings like these can happen fast in either direction.

title: Lesson 60: Why do markets around the world move together?
text: Stock markets in different countries are linked. Big companies sell and buy all over the world, and many investors own stocks in several countries at once. So when a big worry hits one market, it often spreads. On Thursday, AI stocks fell in the U.S. By Friday morning, AI and chip stocks in Japan and South Korea were falling too. That is why owning stocks from many countries does not always protect you on a bad day. Spreading money across different kinds of assets, like stocks and bonds, can help more.
